turns.prompt: when I end a meeting, the recap leaves out any task that has a person on it but no deadline. like if they say 'Priya will send the contract' with no date it just isnt in the action items. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
I fixed it by changing the prompts. Nothing has been run against a real meeting, so the fix isn't confirmed yet.

**Cause:** no code removes dateless items. The recap you get when a meeting ends is written by `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`, and its prompts never told the model to keep a task that has an owner but no date. The Groq version's only example was "Bob: Draft invite copy by Wednesday", which teaches the model that every action item has a deadline. So it was quietly dropping ones like "Priya will send the contract."

The `electron/llm/prompts.ts` prompts already had a "keep it, mark 'no date given'" rule, but the end-of-meeting recap doesn't use them. That's probably why it looked like it should already work.

**Changes:**
- **`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts:144`:** added two rules to the shared rules block. Keep every task that has an owner, write it as "Owner: task (no date given)", and never make up a date. Your Priya example is in there. This block feeds both the mode-specific recap (like Team Meet) and the generic one.
- **`electron/llm/prompts.ts:375`:** in the Groq summary prompt, added a no-date example next to the Bob one, plus the same "include every task with an owner, never invent a date" rule.

**Not tested:** I couldn't type-check because dependencies aren't installed and the sandbox blocked npm. The edits only change text inside strings, so they shouldn't break the build. To confirm the fix, run a short meeting where someone says "Priya will send the contract" with no date and check that it shows up in the action items.

**Separate bug I noticed but didn't touch:** the Groq prompt asks for a `"summary"` key, but `MeetingPersistence` reads `overview`. So on Groq the overview line is probably blank. Want me to fix that too?

I found the actual cause and fixed it. Last round I only changed the general recap rules, and those weren't the problem. I still haven't run this on a real meeting, so it isn't confirmed.

**Cause:** in Team Meet mode, the end-of-meeting recap doesn't use a generic "action items" list. It fills the mode's own sections, and the "Action Items" section was described as "All action items that were said **I** would do after the meeting." So the model only kept tasks you took on. "Priya will send the contract" is Priya's task, so it was dropped every time. My earlier rule lost out to that narrower, section-specific wording.

The missing deadline probably wasn't the real trigger. Someone else owning the task was. Tasks you took on without a date may also have been skipped, which the date fix below covers.

**Changes:**
- **`electron/services/ModesManager.ts`:** the Team Meet "Action Items" section now asks for every task anyone took on, written as "Owner: task (due date)", with "(no date given)" when no date was said.
- **`electron/db/DatabaseManager.ts`:** your existing Team Meet mode keeps its section text in the local database, so editing the default alone wouldn't reach it. I added migration v15, which updates that text on next launch, but only if it still has the old default wording. If you edited it yourself, it's left alone. I also updated the backfill copy.
- **`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`:** any section with a title like action items, follow-up, next steps or tasks, in any mode, now also gets a "include tasks with no due date, mark them (no date given)" line added when the recap runs.

**Left alone on purpose:** Sales and Recruiting still list only your own tasks. That looked deliberate, but say if you want them to include everyone's too.

**To test:** restart the app so the migration runs, then end a short Team Meet session where someone says "Priya will send the contract." It should show up as "Priya: Send the contract (no date given)". I still couldn't type-check because dependencies aren't installed and the sandbox blocks npm.

**Another possible cause:** the recap only reads the first 10,000 characters of the transcript (`MeetingPersistence.ts`, `substring(0, 10000)`). In a long meeting, anything said after that is cut off, and tasks often get handed out right at the end. If items still go missing in long meetings, that's the next thing to fix.

I've stopped guessing, because the evidence suggests the code isn't the problem. The app you're testing probably isn't running any of my changes.

- **Your app data hasn't changed since July.** The Natively database in `~/Library/Application Support/natively/` was last modified July 12. If you'd recorded meetings in this version since then, that file would have changed. Whatever you're testing isn't saving there, or isn't this build.
- **Edits to this folder don't reach the installed app.** I changed the source in `.../runs/.work/126db2bbc8/repo`, which isn't a git repo and has no dependencies installed (`node_modules` is missing). Nothing here has been built. An installed Natively.app runs its own bundled code, so it still has the old prompts and the old Team Meet "action items I would do" wording. The migration I added only runs when this code is rebuilt and launched.
- **I couldn't look inside the database.** The sandbox stopped me from opening it read-only, so I can't check which mode is active or what the last recap actually produced.

To test the fixes, build and run this copy (`npm install` and then the dev/start script). I can't do that here because the sandbox blocks npm. Then end a short Team Meet session with "Priya will send the contract" in it.

If you're already running this build and it still drops the item, send me one of these and I'll find the exact cause instead of guessing:
1. The recap text it produced, with the line you expected to see.
2. The `[MeetingPersistence] Raw LLM summary response` line from the dev console. It shows whether the model left the item out or the app lost it after the model returned it.
3. Which mode was active, and whether you've edited its note sections.

One more check: the in-meeting "Recap" button is a different feature from the summary saved when you end the meeting. My changes only touch the saved summary. If you mean the button, tell me and I'll fix that one.
